paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: faith is trusting God enough to act on what He has said, even when you can't see how it works out. Abraham had the promise, "Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned," and he had the test (Hebrews 11:18). The writer says Abraham "reasoned that God could raise the dead" (Hebrews 11:19). So he didn't throw the promise out. He trusted the One who made it.

Now look at how different these lives were. Some people of faith shut the mouths of lions and quenched raging fire (Hebrews 11:33-34). Others were tortured, mocked, chained, and hid in caves (Hebrews 11:35-38). The writer says that "The world was not worthy of them" (Hebrews 11:38). I think that's the comfort here, baker: faith isn't measured by how things turned out on the outside, because God sees every one of them.

And then the ending, which is my favorite part of the whole letter. "These were all commended for their faith, yet they did not receive what was promised" (Hebrews 11:39). Then comes the good news: "God had planned something better for us, so that together with us they would be made perfect" (Hebrews 11:40). So keep trusting Him today, friend, and keep the ovens warm. You're part of the same family of faith as every name on that list, and it's all headed somewhere good.
